thread:
maria-acme: hey, hitting you because since ~12:09 UTC our text-generation calls started returning very short, garbled outputs. latency spiked from ~120ms to >1.5s and some responses are full of weird token fragments. region=eu-central-1. examples attached. can you check routing?

liam (Support): sorry you're seeing this — can you paste a curl and one example response (raw) and a request id? also which model param are you passing?

maria-acme: curl below. sample response shows tokenization errors (split words, weird unicode). request-id: req_20260317_afe34. model param: redwood-enc4-2b:quantized-v1.

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Region: eu-central-1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-enc4-2b:quantized-v1","input":"Summarize the doc..."}'
```

liam (Support): thanks. I'm seeing our routing logs for req_20260317_afe34 — traffic from your org at 12:09:04 was routed to eu-legacy-enc3-1b (fallback) for ~27s due to a capacity pressure event in the primary pool. legacy-enc3 uses a different tokenizer and vocab, which explains the garbling and capability drop.

maria-acme: ugh — we didn't expect cross-variant fallbacks to be allowed. that explains the hallucinations. can you undo / force traffic back? we have production users impacted. also seeing a token usage spike, will this affect billing?

liam (Support): immediate mitigation: 1) pin the exact model+version in requests (include the full model id with variant) 2) set header `X-Region` to `eu-central-1` to avoid cross-region reroute for now 3) add header `X-Model-Override: redwood-enc4-2b:quantized-v1` as a temporary hard pin. we'll also remove the fallback rule for your org. These are temporary — engineering will patch routing policy. Regarding billing, we'll review the token spike once we have correlated logs and can adjust if caused by the fallback.

sophie (eng-runtime): I'm looking at the policy that triggered fallback — the autoscaler briefly marked the primary pool as degraded and a permissive fallback policy allowed substitution to compatible-capability sets. In this case compatibility was incorrectly judged (quantized enc4 vs legacy enc3) — they are not tokenizer-compatible. Created incident RED-3421 and started a rollback of the permissive rule at 12:35 UTC.

josh (Platform SRE): quick repro if you want to validate locally: send the same prompt to both ids and diff tokens. sample script:

```
# python snippet
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key)
print(c.generate(model='redwood-enc4-2b:quantized-v1', input='hello world') )
print(c.generate(model='eu-legacy-enc3-1b:stable', input='hello world') )
```

liam (Support): i've applied an org-level override to block legacy-enc3 for maria-acme and pushed the temporary header guidance to their workspace. sophie — can you confirm rollback ETA?

sophie (eng-runtime): ETA ~20 minutes to fully revert the permissive fallback and deploy a safe guard: explicit tokenizer compatibility check in the routing decision. I'll post the incident link shortly.

maria-acme: thanks. after adding the X-Model-Override header responses are back to normal. please keep us posted on the incident and any billing adjustments.

sophie (eng-runtime): incident RED-3421 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-3421. root cause: permissive fallback policy + mis-tagged capability metadata for a legacy pool. fix: stricter compatibility checks + unit test to catch tokenizer mismatches. will follow up with postmortem.

deploy-bot: routing-policy-change applied by sophie at 1719999140 : :white_check_mark:

liam (Support): will keep this thread open until postmortem. tagging @billing for the token spike review. :thumbsup:

maria-acme: appreciate the quick response, saving our demo traffic.

josh (Platform SRE): follow-up action: add a canary to ensure fallback never picks a different tokenizer family; ticket RED-3423 created.

sophie (eng-runtime): ok locking down and closing after postmortem. if anyone sees other orgs with same pattern i'll trigger a global mitigation.
